newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel intl calls mart makes "unofficial" debut.
newsitem.headline: Israel intl calls mart makes "unofficial" debut.

text.p: Competition in Israel's international calls market, delayed by squabbles over dialling rates, began in "unofficial" form on Thursday, officials said.
A spokesman for Bezeq Israel Telecom, referring to the two new competitors of the company's international phone service subsidiary, told Reuters:
"We began hooking them up today. We expect to finish hooking up Barak by Sunday, and Golden Lines by Monday."
The competition was to have begun on Tuesday, but was delayed by a dispute between Bezeq and the Communications Ministry over rates.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat on Wednesday accused state-owned Bezeq of violating the law and exploiting its dominant market position after the company published proposed international tariffs, as much as 80 percent below current rates, without ministry approval.
Livnat said Bezeq's international phone service subsidiary was offering customers "dumping prices" and asked Israel's anti-trust authority to intervene.
She also said Bezeq workers were refusing to connect the two new providers, Barak and Golden Lines.
"That is of course an illegal activity which we will deal with," she said.
A ministry spokeswoman said late on Thursday the new providers had begun giving partial service, but that competition would not formally begin until negotiations with Bezeq were completed.
"It is only a matter of days," the spokeswoman said.

Under the law, Bezeq is subject to strict supervision during the first six months of the new competitive market. Bezeq said the ministry knew of its ad campaign and that it had not violated the law because the new rates were not yet in force.
Golden Lines is controlled by SBC Communications Inc, Italy's Stet and three Israeli partners.
Barak is controlled by Sprint Corp , France Telecom , Deutsche Telekom , Clal Israel and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
Livnat said that as a result of the competition a call to the United States will drop from around 3.50 shekels a minute to 0.70-0.80 shekels a minute.
